rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

agent.problem: Story cards 3, 9, 11 and 13 all exceed two sentences. Only the opening card may run to three sentences; each later story card must be compressed to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: Nothing on the earlier cards indicates how the hearers respond to Jesus' teaching. Astonished, unmoved and silent are all compatible with that setup, so the blank asks for an unseen reaction rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: No earlier card names or hints at Jesus' mother. Knowing that the crowd mentions His trade and family does not let the baker reason out Mary rather than Elizabeth or Martha, so this blank depends on prior knowledge or luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The opening clause retells Jesus taking the little girl by the hand and her getting up, which is Mark 5:41-42, but the card cites only Mark 6:5. Its citation is narrower than the Bible content it tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: The preceding cards do not establish Jesus' emotional response to the unbelief. Amazed, angry and grieved are all plausible reactions to the setup, so the baker cannot reason out the blank from what has been shown.

agent.problem: Cards 2, 7 and 14 already provide several discovery questions whose answers cannot be deduced from the setup. Cards 4, 8 and 15 add three more pure guesses, leaving only four of the ten choice cards as reasoned picks. Discovery questions therefore make up most of the stop rather than the allowed few.

rule.text: Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
